items.readable_text:
Content:
Recall that Euler's number, denoted [MATH: e,] is an irrational number whose decimal approximation is
[MATH: e\approx2.718\,281\,828.]

Content:
As we'll discover, the exponential growth curve [MATH: y=e^x] is one of the most important curves in mathematics. Its graph is given below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/cec84ef9213a04defabd1ee37f12b017]

Content:
Now, suppose we want to sketch the graph of [MATH: y=e^{x-3} + 1.]

Content:
First, we shift it [MATH: 3] units to the right to get [MATH: y=e^{x-3}.] The [MATH: y]-intercept moves from [MATH: (0,1)] to the point [MATH: (3,1)] but the horizontal asymptote stays at [MATH: y=0.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/d84b038faef6126fa2b35598925f6d38]

Content:
Then, we vertically shift it by [MATH: 1] unit up to give [MATH: e^{x-3} + 1.] The point [MATH: (3,1)] moves to [MATH: (3,2)] and the horizontal asymptote moves from [MATH: y=0] to [MATH: y=1.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/481ea97692c89ad7c586681f09060294]

sections.normalized_html:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

  • First, we plot the graph of [MATH: y=8^x.]

  • To plot [MATH: y=8^{x+2},] we shift the graph of [MATH: y=8^{x}] horizontally by [MATH: 2] units to the left. The [MATH: y]-intercept moves from [MATH: (0,1)] to [MATH: (-2,1),] but the horizontal asymptote stays at [MATH: y=0.]

  • To plot [MATH: y=8^{x+2}-4,] we shift the graph of [MATH: y=8^{x+2}] vertically by [MATH: 4] units down. The point [MATH: (-2,1)] moves to [MATH: (-2,-3)] and the horizontal asymptote moves from [MATH: y=0] to [MATH: y=-4.]

sections.normalized_html:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

  • We take the curve [MATH: y=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^x.]

  • Horizontally shift it by [MATH: 4] units to the right to give [MATH: y=\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x-4}.] The [MATH: y]-intercept moves from [MATH: (0,1)] to [MATH: (4,1)] but the horizontal asymptote stays at [MATH: y=0.]

  • Then, reflect it on the [MATH: x]-axis to give [MATH: y=-\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{x-4}.] The point [MATH: (4,1)] moves to [MATH: (4,-1)] and the horizontal asymptote stays at [MATH: y=0.]
